title: E-Math trigonometry: ratios and the sine rule
subject: math
strengths: Most of the class can name the opposite, adjacent and hypotenuse for angle theta in the 3-4-5 triangle.
The class can pair a side with the sine of its opposite angle when setting up the sine rule.

modelAnswers.question: Write out the SOH CAH TOA card in full, and use it to state cos theta for the 3-4-5 triangle.
modelAnswers.answer: SOH: sin = opposite / hypotenuse. CAH: cos = adjacent / hypotenuse. TOA: tan = opposite / adjacent. So cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8.

modelAnswers.question: In triangle ABC, side a = 4 is opposite angle A = 30 degrees, and angle B = 60 degrees. Use the sine rule to find side b, showing your working.
modelAnswers.answer: a / sin A = b / sin B, so 4 / sin 30 degrees = b / sin 60 degrees. Then b = (4 x sin 60 degrees) / sin 30 degrees = (4 x 0.8660) / 0.5, so b is about 6.93.

commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that tan theta is 4/3, putting the adjacent side on top.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: name the opposite and adjacent sides for theta first, then read TOA aloud and rewrite the ratio.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected working: TOA puts the opposite on top, so the tangent ratio uses the side across from theta over the side next to it.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks 4/3 for tan theta and defends it by pointing at the side next to theta.

fixIt.prompt: Fix it: swap the top and bottom of the flipped ratio and check the size of the result against the whole.
fixIt.corrected: Corrected check: the flipped 4/3 is taller than the whole, while the correct TOA ratio is a proper part of it.

nextSteps: Reteach the trap, landing that TOA reads opposite first, adjacent second, and that naming the sides comes before any ratio is written.
Practise the sine-rule pairing from the worked example - substitute the known side-angle pair first, then rearrange for the unknown side.
